tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_files
tools.description: Publish an artifact from files on disk: their bytes go from the files to the artifact and do not pass through you. Prefer this to publish_version when the page's files already exist, when there is more than one file or an image, or when the page is large. For each file give `as`, the path it is served at, and `path`, its absolute path on the machine where your own file tools run; leave `uri` out. index.html is required in a new artifact. Limits for one call: 256 files, 20 MiB a file, 64 MiB in all. The client may refuse a file it will not send, such as a secrets file, a link or a path outside the working folder. Omit slug to create an artifact, private to you. To republish, give slug and base_version (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish); title and icon are kept when omitted. A republish changes only the files named and keeps the rest, which stay served: to take a file away, list it in remove. mode "replace" makes the files named the whole artifact and drops the rest. This tool publishes only to an artifact of yours. **Files Claude did not write**: Claude reads the whole file before publishing it, even when the person asks it not to. Publishing distributes the content, and Claude never distributes what it has not seen. A request for privacy is a reason to read before publishing, not an exemption. If Claude cannot read the file, it does not publish it. **Claude never publishes** a page that impersonates a real person or organization, for example by using their name, branding, byline or domain. Claude also never publishes fabricated records, receipts or reviews presented as genuine, forms or flows that collect credentials or payment details under false pretenses, or content that targets a private individual. Claude refuses whether it wrote the page or the person supplied it, and whatever purpose is claimed, such as a prop or a test, when the page would work as the real thing. If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.

artifact_title.description: The artifact's current title, as get_artifact gives it. Needed when shared_live is 'public'.

contract.description: Optional runtime-contract version. Leave it out to keep the current one.

Required when that value is 'users' (named people or groups), 'org' (the user's whole organization) or 'public' (anyone with the link). Leave it out for a new artifact and when the value is 'owner'. slug.description: The artifact's slug. Omit to create a new artifact.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_version
tools.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. Some clients may publish only to your own artifacts: there the call is refused as owner-only. Republishing is read-then-send: base_version must name the live version you are replacing (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result) — if it is no longer live, the publish is rejected with a conflict; re-read and retry from the current state. On success the new version goes live immediately. When republishing, the artifact's stored connectors manifest carries forward unchanged, and so do title, favicon, icon and contract when omitted. Content is capped at 16 MiB.

schema.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_version
schema.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. Some clients may publish only to your own artifacts: there the call is refused as owner-only. Republishing is read-then-send: base_version must name the live version you are replacing (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result) — if it is no longer live, the publish is rejected with a conflict; re-read and retry from the current state. On success the new version goes live immediately. When republishing, the artifact's stored connectors manifest carries forward unchanged, and so do title, favicon, icon and contract when omitted. Content is capped at 16 MiB.

artifact_title.description: The artifact's current title, as get_artifact gives it. Needed when shared_live is 'public'.

base_version.description: Required when slug is given: the version id this publish replaces — echo the version get_artifact or read_artifact returned (or your last publish result's). Rejected with a conflict if it no longer names the live version, so concurrent edits are never silently overwritten. Omit when creating.

content.description: The complete HTML document, at most 16 MiB. Must sniff as text/html — begin it with <!DOCTYPE html>.

contract.description: Optional runtime-contract version (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Leave it out to keep the current one. Pass one only when the user asks for a different version, or this server's answer says to. If the publish is rejected because the contract is yanked or out of the supported window, republish with an explicit "0.0.0" to clear the contract — omitting the argument is not a reliable recovery (the server may carry the stored contract forward, repeating the rejection).

deadline.description: Optional, rarely needed: by when pages still open on an OLDER version must have moved to this one — one word: now, 15m, 1h, 24h, 7d, or an ISO-8601 time at most 30 days ahead. Omit it for ordinary edits (open pages then move at their next quiet moment); it cannot be relaxed once published.

favicon.description: Optional legacy emoji marker; omit it.

icon.description: One short, generic word for the artifact's tab icon — a plain signifier of what it is, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map; not a product or brand name. Pass one when creating; omit when republishing to keep the current icon.

shared_live.description: States who the artifact you are republishing is already shared with, and changes nothing: its 'read' value from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result. Required when that value is 'users' (named people or groups), 'org' (the user's whole organization) or 'public' (anyone with the link). Leave it out for a new artifact and when the value is 'owner'. Rejected if it does not match the artifact's current value.

slug.description: The artifact's server-assigned slug (UUID), e.g. from list_artifacts, get_artifact or the artifact's own URL. Omit to create a new artifact.

title.description: Browser-tab title. Required when creating. When republishing it is optional — omitted, the new version keeps the current live version's title (the server also keeps the stored HTML's <title> element in sync with it); pass a value only to rename the artifact, never invent a new title on a routine republish.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__read_artifact
tools.description: Read the current document of an artifact: one that the user owns, or one that belongs to someone in the user's organization and that the user can open. Read a pasted claude.ai artifact link with this tool. Returns a JSON summary (slug, version id, title, favicon, runtime-contract version, total_lines, and for a multi-file artifact its file names), then the HTML of the version the user is served, then a reminder. The HTML, and the summary's title, favicon and file names, are wrapped in an <untrusted-document-...> tag that the summary's notice names; the tag is not part of them. A document over ~1 MiB is not served whole: read it in parts with offset and limit, which count lines; next_offset says where the next part starts. ## Rule 1: Cost Confirmation
Before calling ANY tool that costs credits, ask which ai_model to use where there is a choice (prefer an explicit one), present the cost and wait for user confirmation.

| Tool | Credits |
|------|---------|

| meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d | table below |
| meshy_text_to_3d_refine / meshy_retexture | 10 (15 with texture_resolution "8k") |
| meshy_remesh / meshy_rig (incl. walking + running) / meshy_uv_unwrap | 5 |
| meshy_animate | 3 per action |
| meshy_text_to_motion | 10 (prime) / 3 (swift) |
| meshy_repair_printability / meshy_process_multicolor / meshy_auto_split | 10 |
| meshy_convert / meshy_resize | 1 |
| meshy_creative_lab | 36; keycap 62; fidget-collapsible 6 |

| analyze printability, balance, usage, animation library, status, list, download | free |

| image / multi-image ai_model | mesh only | + 2K/4K texture | + 8K texture |
|---|---|---|---|

If a create call fails with a timeout, network error or 5xx, the task may still have been created and charged. Check meshy_list_tasks (task_type = that task's type) for it before calling the create tool again. A wait that times out leaves the task running: poll the same task_id again.

target_formats is fixed at creation time (3mf only when listed), so ask about the intended use first.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.
- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

# Re-review rulings — 2026-10-27 (delegated: the user said "just use best judgment")

Marker for every edit that applies one of these: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling Rn)*.
In-text record where a decision is stated: "Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling Rn (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): ..."
These rulings never reverse a prior user ruling; they settle consequences the user's rulings left ambiguous or unimplementable.

## General rules (G)
- G1 Owner wins: where two GDDs disagree on a value, field, unit or contract, the registry `source:` GDD wins and the other conforms. If the thing is unregistered, the PUBLISHER of the field/signal/value wins and the consumer conforms.
- G2 Specialist disagreements: follow the creative-director's stated resolution in that GDD's disagreements list. Where the CD said "the user should choose", take the CD's stated lean.
- G3 Carried-over blockers (flagged "still not fixed"/"carried over"): previous edits did not land. After each edit, Grep for the old wording and confirm it is gone everywhere in the GDD (body, examples, ACs, tuning tables, OQs).
- G4 ACs that contradict the GDD's own formulas: recompute from the formula at registry defaults; never weaken a formula to match an AC.
- G5 Division/overflow at boundaries: guard explicitly (e.g. avail == 0 -> share 0, everything unserved); state the guard in the formula and add a boundary AC.

## Cross-cutting rulings (R)
- R1 Restore epoch (consequence of X8/D16). Save/Load OWNS `restore_epoch` as a persisted integer in the save slot header (u32, starts 0). The kernel exposes it read-only in `kernel.clock` as (T, world_seed, restore_epoch) — sim-visible, pure. The KERNEL (command-simulation-layer.md) owns the one derivation for threat draws, counter_eff = rng_counter + RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE x restore_epoch, and owns RESTORE_KEY_STRIDE (value 1048576 unchanged; registry_request: move its source from attention-system.md to command-simulation-layer.md, with attention, horror and save-load in referenced_by). The stream name hash stays cached and unchanged. Attention and Horror call the kernel derivation; neither defines its own. Graph physical failures and persisted counters never read the epoch. Determinism (G3/G4) is defined given (save bytes, restore_epoch): the same pair replays identically; tests pin the epoch. Required ACs: (i) two successive restores of the same save yield epochs e and e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) a fresh-process reload of the same slot also advances the epoch; (iii) same (save, epoch) pair -> identical draws. Save/Load's 'none of it able to alter the sim' is amended to exempt restore_epoch.
- R2 seq (kernel CR-4). The kernel stamps `seq` internally per (peer, source); callers never choose it; `submit()` stays void (fire-and-forget). A caller may attach an opaque `correlation` field (int) that the kernel echoes unchanged in the result/rejection event. Player Controller keys pre-play tokens by `correlation`. Update the kernel seq ACs (L883, L892, L902-904) and PC-7 together.
- R3 Completion sentinel (kernel CR-19b). Every owner callable receives `ctx`; results flow through ctx, never the return value: validate reports via ctx.ok() / ctx.reject(reason); snapshot via ctx.put(payload); apply(cmd, write_scope, ctx). Every callable's only return is `return ctx.complete()` (a typed token). No `-> void` owner callables.

The Pipeline PUBLISHES f_q. Aim direction = cursor_aim_world - AIM_ORIGIN, with AIM_ORIGIN = floor(pos) + (0, AIM_ORIGIN_Y) (ruling D10); remove the chest-based subtraction from the Pipeline's D.14b/D.7. Pace-robustness, scoped to that salvage carry only: (a) while a salvage carry is held, attention decay is suspended (freezing with cargo is priced, per X3); (b) dropping and re-taking the same item grants no fresh TELL_REARM immunity (the rearm timer keys on the item, not the pickup). User ruling D16 ("not steerable by quit") outranks delegated R1. A **death-stub restore** advances `restore_epoch` (durably, R14). A **Continue** that restores a `QUIT` generation which is the newest non-demoted verified generation **carries the epoch unchanged** (no epoch write). A Continue of any other generation (after a kill, crash or fallback) advances it. ACs: (i) death restore -> e+1 and different threat draws; (ii) Save & Quit, Continue -> same epoch, identical draws; (iii) kill, Continue of an AUTO/EVENT generation -> e+1; (iv) same (save, epoch) -> identical draws.

## R14 Where the epoch lives and when it is durable (fixes kernel CR-15 vs SL-23 and the REBASED-key/trailer-SHA defect)
- `restore_epoch` is stored in a **per-slot side file** `slot_epoch.bin` (u32 + CRC32), written atomically (temp file + rename) by the Save/Load worker. It is **not** in any generation file, so generation bytes and every trailer SHA and every key derived from them never change.
- When an advance is due (R13), Save/Load issues the epoch write in a **pre-restore staging step, before calling `request_restore`**, polls it per frame (never blocks the main thread), and calls `request_restore(gen, restore_epoch)` only after `EPOCH_DURABLE`. The kernel's LOADING stays atomic within one boundary service. Kernel CR-15 is reworded to: "Save/Load's epoch staging step has completed (EPOCH_DURABLE, or a logged SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE with save_status = FAILED)", and the kernel lists the failure-path exposure too.
- If the write fails or exceeds `RESTORE_EPOCH_WRITE_MAX_MS` (500 ms placeholder), the restore proceeds with the advanced epoch in memory, logs `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` and sets `save_status = FAILED` (the device is failing; saving is impossible anyway). This is a **listed exposure**: a kill before any later successful write may replay that epoch once. The ACs for durability are scoped to the success path; the failure path has its own AC (logged, status FAILED, play continues).
- A missing or corrupt `slot_epoch.bin` reads as `max(epoch recorded in the newest generation's header copy, 0) + 1`. Each generation header also records the epoch at write time (read-only copy, for recovery).

Where a locked formula belongs to another GDD the Overlay **cites it by name and never re-expresses it with other numbers**: `step_over_budget` and `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4 ("a threshold, not a cap", kern D.6), `state_hash` (kern D.12), `log_coverage_ticks` (kern D.13, `COMMAND_LOG_CAPACITY` 1024), `lag_ticks` (kern:351, repeated only in the form the kernel publishes it), and the Filter's return path (pf D.6). # Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"
- Dependencies must be bidirectional — if system A depends on B, B's doc must mention A
- Tuning knobs must specify safe ranges and what gameplay aspect they affect
- Acceptance criteria must be testable — a QA tester must be able to verify pass/fail
- No hand-waving: "the system should feel good" is not a valid specification
- Balance values must link to their source formula or rationale
- Design documents MUST be written incrementally: create skeleton first, then fill
  each section one at a time with user approval between sections. Write each
  approved section to the file immediately to persist decisions and manage context

462	## Formulas
463	
464	**Scope and determinism.** The Overlay defines **nine** formula blocks (the ruling's eight formulas, with `graph_hook_tick` and `hook_window_p99` registered separately), and all nine are display arithmetic: none is hashed, replicated, saved or read by a simulation system, and none can change `state_hash` (DO-9). Where the inputs are integers (every Graph, Suit and kernel quantity is an integer unit, `mC`, `mGU`, `dkPa`, `permille`, `bp`, ticks, runs, microseconds) the arithmetic is integer, with explicit floor and ceiling, so the table-driven tests of the classifier and the percentile are exact and identical on every machine. Where a locked formula belongs to another GDD the Overlay **cites it by name and never re-expresses it with other numbers**: `step_over_budget` and `STEP_BUDGET_MS` 4 ("a threshold, not a cap", kern D.6), `state_hash` (kern D.12), `log_coverage_ticks` (kern D.13, `COMMAND_LOG_CAPACITY` 1024), `lag_ticks` (kern:351, repeated only in the form the kernel publishes it), and the Filter's return path (pf D.6). Every `DIAG_*` / `OVERLAY_*` value below is a `[PLACEHOLDER]` with a range in Tuning Knobs. Proposed registry names for the merge stage (written from this final text, never from a draft): `desync_classifier`, `graph_hook_tick`, `hook_window_p99`, `dirty_load_pm`, `queue_load_pm`, `ticks_per_overlay_refresh`, `overlay_cpu_us`, `hash_cost_per_s`, `stage_entry_latency_s`. The nine blocks below are the ruling's eight formulas (R30's six, plus `queue_load_pm`, plus `stage_entry_latency_s`), with the pair "`graph_hook_tick` and `hook_window_p99`" written as two blocks (F-2, F-3) because the registry names them separately. **Determinism across frame rates** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the classifier and every counter are functions of kernel ticks and of the class folds (DO-21 (5)), never of the rendered frame rate, the refresh throttle or `Engine.time_scale`; the same `T` gives the same class at 20, 60 and 144 fps, within one fold interval (12 ticks) or exactly in tick-driven mode (AC-DO-156).
465	
466	### F-1. `desync_classifier`
467	
468	The `desync_classifier` formula is defined as:
469	
470	`class(ref, viewer) = first_match(row_1 ... row_9 of the DO-21 class table)`, evaluated at each class fold (DO-21 (5): at most once per Sanity run, independent of `DIAG_REFRESH_HZ`) from the fold's own same-frame read of `(tv, p, ledger row, lie_intent, Filter counters)`; the numeral refresh only displays the latest fold *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*
471	
472	The sub-expressions the rows use (all integers in the **owner's unit** of the ref: `mC`, `mGU`, `dkPa`, `permille`, `bp`; binary-frame refs compare as 0 or 1) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix: `sanity_listed`, `live_row`, `subject_rows`, `scope`, `ledger_active`, `dT` and `n_eq`; `dT` also delegated ruling R13)*:
473	
474	```
475	binary_frame(ref) : if true, span, arc_deg and q_display are NOT consulted (a binary-frame ref has no PF-45 dial calibration): q_display is unset, tol_eff = 0, p_int = the displayed frame state (0 or 1), disc = 0 if p_int == tv else 1, step_enabled = false, and no check below returns UNAVAILABLE / NO_RESOLVER for a missing span or arc. binary_frame is true for STATE_GLYPH, HOUSING_GLOW, MACHINE_FRAME and any ref carrying a SPRITE_SWAP lie (DO-21)
476	span          = value_hi - value_lo                             # needle and readout refs only (skipped when binary_frame(ref)); > 0 and arc_deg > 0, else UNAVAILABLE / NO_RESOLVER; from the PF-45 calibration
477	floor_div(a,b)= a div b rounded toward minus infinity           # GDScript int '/' truncates toward zero: use floori(float(a) / b) or a sign-corrected form
478	p_int         = displayed frame state (0 or 1)                  if binary_frame(ref)            # no span, arc or q_display is read
479	              = p.displayed_value                               if p.motion_mode == HONEST      # honest path: exact and an integer by the Filter contract, never rounded
480	              = floor_div(value_lo * 1000 + span * p.displayed_pm + 500, 1000)   otherwise      # integer arithmetic from the integer displayed_pm; half rounds up, for negative values too
481	disc          = abs(p_int - tv)                                 # binary-frame refs: 0 if equal else 1
482	q_display     = ceil_div(span, 1000)                            # owner's units, >= 1; from the PF-45 calibration (published by the Filter, registry `filter_counters`); unset when binary_frame(ref)
483	tol_eff       = max(tol(kind), q_display)                       # if q_display is unpublished or binary_frame(ref): tol_eff = tol(kind), which is 0 for a binary-frame ref
484	step_enabled  = (q_display is published)                        # a RETURN exists only for a calibrated ref (PF-44), so this is true whenever it matters
485	target        = lie_targets(ref)                                # published by the Filter (the PF-9 bijection ref <-> subject_ref {stable_id, surface}, plus the ref's quantity), or NONE
486	sanity_listed(row) = ledger_listed(viewer, row.lie_id)             # Sanity's DIAGNOSTIC accessor (SN-23): true iff the row is in sanity.perception for the seat this run, i.e. the row is ACTIVE, in the seat's compartment or `away` (every ACTIVE row is listed, SN-23 as amended 2026-10-28); the Overlay never reads sanity.perception. This is the ONLY use of lie_id in the join (membership); the match itself is still by (viewer, subject_ref, surface/quantity), never by lie_id
487	live_row(row)      = row.viewer == viewer and row.state == ACTIVE and sanity_listed(row)   # an ACTIVE row is live whether or not the seat is in its compartment (`away`, EC-SN-35); a listing that disagrees with ACTIVE is never guessed (it would only arise from a Sanity defect)
488	subject_rows(ref)  = { r : live_row(r) and r.subject_ref.stable_id == the stable_id of the ref's PF-9 subject }   # needs the ref-to-subject mapping only, not lie_targets
489	scope         = NONE            if the ref has no ref-to-subject mapping (PF-9)                                                                    # UNAVAILABLE / NO_RESOLVER
490	              = NONE            if ledger_listed is unpublished and the subject has >= 1 row in state ACTIVE for the viewer                       # UNAVAILABLE / NO_RESOLVER (the listing is unknown, never a guess)
491	              = RESOLVED        if |subject_rows(ref)| == 0                                                                                       # vacuous join: no live row on the subject, so ledger_active is false for EVERY ref of it whatever lie_targets says; this is the end-of-lie case (the ledger row ended, the Filter's lie_id lags one run)
492	              = RESOLVED        if target is published, or the ref's subject has exactly one ref
493	              = SUBJECT_SCOPE   if target is unpublished or ambiguous, the subject has more than one ref and |subject_rows(ref)| == 1           # the one degradation rule (E-DO-49 and AC-DO-163 cite it)
494	              = NONE            if target is unpublished or ambiguous, the subject has more than one ref and |subject_rows(ref)| >= 2              # UNAVAILABLE / NO_RESOLVER, never a guess
495	              (evaluated in this order, first match wins)
496	ledger_active = (scope == RESOLVED and exists r in subject_rows(ref) with r.subject_ref == target's {stable_id, surface} (and the quantity where the PF-9 triple carries one; a single-ref subject matches on stable_id))
497	                or scope == SUBJECT_SCOPE                           # lowest (start_run, lie_id) wins among matches (PF-46); SUBJECT_SCOPE is subject granularity: true for EVERY ref of the subject, none asserted verified
498	unverified    = scope == SUBJECT_SCOPE or not intent_published      # row 6 then shows the tag UNVERIFIED (why: SUBJECT_SCOPE or INTENT_UNKNOWN), never LIE
499	fold          = at most one per change of run (T crosses a multiple of SANITY_DRIFT_DIVISOR = 12); independent of DIAG_REFRESH_HZ, the throttle, fps and Engine.time_scale
500	dT            = min(T_fold - T_prev_fold, SANITY_DRIFT_DIVISOR + MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME - 1)   # ticks: 12 normally, up to 15 on a catch-up frame; 0 means no fold and no counter moves (PAUSED). On the FIRST fold of a session and on a restore (a LOADING -> RUNNING edge since the previous fold (DO-32), or T < T_prev_fold, or a change of kernel.clock restore_epoch): dT = 0 and every counter and anchor clears. The LOADING edge is the signal that never misses: a Continue of the newest QUIT generation carries restore_epoch unchanged and restores a T that need not be below T_prev_fold (delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14), so the epoch is corroboration only, neither sufficient nor necessary (Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R13; cross-GDD fix)
501	lie_age       = run - active_run                            # runs since activation; Sanity runs at TICK_RATE / SANITY_DRIFT_DIVISOR = 60 / 12 = 5 per s
502	reach_age     = ceil_div(GLIDE_REACH_FRAC_pm * (end_run - active_run), 1000)    # GLIDE_REACH_FRAC 0.6 -> 600 pm; binary-frame refs: SWAP_LEAD_S * 5; +infinity when end_run <= active_run (an unset end_run never reaches the gate). A lie shorter than reach_age + DIAG_SILENT_LIE_GRACE_TICKS cannot be assessed and reads ONSET for its life (Sanity's minimum life is 200 runs, so this is out of contract)
503	onset         = silent_ok and (lie_age < reach_age or (disc <= tol_eff and n_eq <= DIAG_SILENT_LIE_GRACE_TICKS))   # the exact ONSET predicate (AC-DO-24 to AC-DO-30 agree): the departure has not yet had its age, or it has and is still inside the grace
504	d_int_u       = floor_div(lie_intent.d_intended_pm * span + 500, 1000)           # the Filter's intended departure in the owner's unit; binary-frame refs: 1 if not_drawn == NONE else 0
505	silent_ok     = intent_published and lie_intent.not_drawn == NONE and not lie_intent.short_reach and d_int_u > tol_eff
506	n_eq          = n_eq_prev   + dT  if (scope == RESOLVED and ledger_active and lie_age >= reach_age and disc <= tol_eff and silent_ok) else 0         # ticks, at a fold; 0 whenever no live row matches (the lie_age / reach_age inputs exist only while the row is ACTIVE)
507	n_skew        = n_skew_prev + dT  if (scope == RESOLVED and (ledger_active XOR (lie_id != 0 and motion_mode != RETURN)) and lie_intent.not_drawn == NONE) else 0   # ticks
508	n_diff        = n_diff_prev + 1   if (lie_id == 0 and not ledger_active and motion_mode != RETURN and p_int != tv) else 0     # FOLDS, not ticks; see row_9
509	n_leak        = n_leak_prev + dT  if (lie_id != 0 and motion_mode != RETURN and leak_probe_present and drawn_leak(ref) == 0 and p.leak_amplitude_pm >= floor_eff)   # floor_eff = stage-indexed AMP_FLOOR_PM, 400/325/250 at stages 0-1/2/3 else 0   # ticks
510	t_ret         = (T - T_ret_start) / TICK_RATE  seconds         # ticks, not frames: freezes when the kernel is PAUSED
511	progress      = sign(tv - p_int_prev) * (p_int - p_int_prev)    # the displayed value moved toward the true value this fold (owner's unit; negative = away)
512	T_stall       = T_fold if progress >= q_display else T_stall    # starts at T_ret_start; re-anchored while the follower is still following
513	t_stall       = (T - T_stall) / TICK_RATE                       # seconds without progress, ticks-based
514	closing(t)    = if binary_frame(ref):               disc == 0
515	                elif t_ret <  WANDER_BLEND_S:       disc_t <= disc_end + abs(tv_t - tv_end) + tol_eff               # envelope
516	                elif step_enabled:                  disc_t <= disc_prev + abs(tv_t - tv_prev) + q_display          # step test at fold cadence; slack is the display quantum
517	                                                    and ( t_ret < WANDER_BLEND_S + DIAG_RETURN_WINDOW_TICKS / TICK_RATE
518	                                                          or sum(progress over the last DIAG_RETURN_WINDOW_TICKS) >= min(DIAG_RETURN_FLOOR_QD * q_display, disc_win) )   # windowed progress floor; disc_win = disc at the window start
519	                else:                               true                                                            # held by the stall bound only
520	row_1  UNAVAILABLE        if any input is missing (reasons: NOT_RUNNING, SETTLING, REMOTE_VIEWER, NO_LEDGER, NO_RESOLVER, NO_TRUE_SOURCE, and the row_9 case MEMO_UNCONFIRMED)
521	row_2  SKEW               if scope == RESOLVED and n_skew >= 1 and n_skew <= DIAG_SKEW_GRACE_TICKS
522	row_3  DEFECT_NO_LEAK     if lie_id != 0 and motion_mode != RETURN and ( (leak_modes & GLEAM) == 0                  # tripwire on PF-15
523	                                                                         or (d_leak_repaired > 0 and lie_id == leak_repaired_lie_id)   # only when the Filter publishes the repaired lie's id (OQ-DO-26 (A)); leak_repaired is a GLOBAL counter, so otherwise one page-level UNATTRIBUTED event per counter edge, never a per-ref class
524	                                                                         or n_leak > DIAG_NO_LEAK_GRACE_TICKS )      # the gleam was asked for and never drawn (probe)
525	row_4  DEFECT_SILENT_LIE  if scope == RESOLVED and ledger_active and intent_published and ( (lie_id != 0 and n_eq > DIAG_SILENT_LIE_GRACE_TICKS)
526	                                                                      or (lie_id == 0 and lie_intent.not_drawn == NONE and n_skew > DIAG_SKEW_GRACE_TICKS) )
527	row_5  DEFECT_BYPASS      if probe_present and abs(drawn_mdeg - angle_mdeg(p.displayed_pm)) > LEAK_EPS_MDEG   # integer millidegrees, pre-snap, inclusive
528	row_6  DELIBERATE         if ledger_active and ( (lie_id != 0 and (leak_modes & GLEAM) != 0) or (lie_id == 0 and (lie_intent.not_drawn != NONE or not intent_published)) or scope == SUBJECT_SCOPE )   # (not row_4); second tag NO_NEEDLE > SHORT_REACH > SUB_TOL > ONSET (onset predicate above); the DISPLAY tag is LIE only when not unverified, and UNVERIFIED (why SUBJECT_SCOPE or INTENT_UNKNOWN) replaces LIE when unverified: missing verification is never mapped to the verified class

530	row_8  HONEST             if not ledger_active and (lie_id == 0 or motion_mode == RETURN) and p_int == tv            # exact equality of integers, never tol; a closed return (p_int == tv) is HONEST
531	row_9  DEFECT_UNCAUSED    otherwise (with a why sub-tag); a result whose why is NO_LEDGER_DIFF is shown as UNAVAILABLE / MEMO_UNCONFIRMED until n_diff >= DIAG_NO_LEDGER_DIFF_FOLDS (2), because on a fold frame the Overlay's perceived() call may be the first evaluation, not a memo hit, and a memo filled before the tick notification would give a one-frame false defect (OQ-DO-28)                                                              # the catch-all: no input falls through

# Design Document Rules

- The 8 GDD sections are: Overview, Player Fantasy, Detailed Rules, Formulas, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Tuning Knobs, Acceptance Criteria
- **How many are required depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`, 5 (+ Formulas when the system **defines numeric rules**: rates, curves, thresholds, costs, damage, drop weights — anything a balance pass would tune) at `standard`, none at `minimal` (the design record there is `design/game-brief.md`). Resolve the tier before flagging a section as missing; see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`
- **The Formulas test is what the system defines, not what it is called.** A system's `Category` in `systems-index.md` is a hint — `Gameplay`, `Economy` and `Progression` almost always qualify — never the test. Do not gate Formulas on a category token: the categories `/map-systems` writes (`Core · Gameplay · Progression · Economy · Persistence · UI · Audio · Narrative · Meta`) do not include `combat` or `AI`, which are example systems *within* `Gameplay`. Every site stating this rule must state the same test.
- **Section-name alias**: The GDD template and `/design-system` author this section as `## Detailed Design`; the design standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. These are the SAME required section — accept either heading and never rewrite one into the other.
- Formulas must include variable definitions, expected value ranges, and example calculations
- Edge cases must explicitly state what happens, not just "handle gracefully"

23

47	
48	*Indirect: the player never meets this system, and never will. They meet a promise it lets the studio keep.* (The register is the kernel's, kern:30. Two audiences are kept apart: the **player's** fantasy is written here, as trust; the **operator's** experience, the developer, QA or playtest observer who actually uses the tool, is written in Game Feel.)
49	
50	**Every lie was meant, and every lie leaks.** The scrubber gauge in derelict A reads a calm OK while frost thickens on the elbow beside it. The player has to choose what to believe, and the game owes them one thing: the choice must be *fair*. The frost must be the ship, the gauge must be the dream, and the dream must show its seam somewhere (a gleam on the needle, a glide a real needle would not make). Pillar 1: the physical world is ground truth, only instruments and perception can be wrong. Pillar 4: no lie is unfalsifiable, and at least one channel of truth always remains.
51	
52	A defect breaks that promise silently. A gauge that reads wrong because a value went stale, a rendering path skipped the Filter, or a co-op peer drifted out of step looks *exactly* like a hallucination to the player, but it has no cause, no leak and no way to be disproved. To the player that is not horror; it is the game cheating. The kernel says it plainly: "The fantasy has failed if any player-visible physical consequence ever disagrees with the authoritative state. That is a Pillar 1 violation, not a cosmetic bug — and the reason the Debug Overlay exists" (kern:42).
53	
54	So the player's fantasy here is **trust in the doubt**: the confidence, earned across sorties, that suspicion is always worth acting on, because the world will answer. The Overlay is the instrument that earns it on the player's behalf. It puts the true value beside the perceived one and gives every difference a name (a lie, a returning lie, or a defect), so the studio can prove each lie was issued and leaked, and that each instrument's discrepancy matches its ledger entry, before any player has to take it on faith. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: narrowed. The Overlay checks instrument discrepancies. It has no probe for the physical consequence itself, the frost on the elbow or the hiss at the seam, so it cannot prove that each consequence agreed with the ship; that probe is logged as OQ-DO-27.)*
55	
56	**Emotion target, across a player's run (what the Overlay protects, not what it adds):** *suspicion* (the snag in the reading) -> *a check that costs something* (walk to the elbow, feel the cold) -> *the world answers* -> *trust in the doubt* (next time the player acts on the snag sooner). This extends the Filter's arc (pf:59: "familiarity -> the snag -> suspicion with a direction -> quiet certainty -> trained eye"); the Overlay adds no emotion of its own to a run, it guarantees that the last two steps are never false.
57	
58	**Corollary, the operator** *(the one sane seat aboard)*: the Overlay is the only place that sees both the ship and the dream. It is flat, unlit and plain, and it never lies, because it sits above the pass that does (pipe:102; pf:223 row 9). Its emotion arc is a report ("the gauge lied and I could not tell") -> reproduction -> classification in one glance (a named class, not a judgement call) -> certainty: a lie with a ledger entry and a leak is design, anything else is a ticket (written out in Game Feel).
59	
60	**Rejected, by name, so nobody re-proposes it:** a "true sight" toggle, streamer mode, assist option or launch flag for curious players. An honest overlay over a lying HUD makes Pillar 4 switchable off (R-7, ab:886), and it fails six already-written release-export file-list acceptance criteria (kern:916, pipe:1028, AC-PF-79, player-controller-input.md:1071, AC-AT-66, AC-SN-85). 131	## Detailed Design
132	
133	### Core Rules
134	
135	**Conventions.** Rules are `DO-n` (named); edge cases are `E-DO-nn`, acceptance criteria `AC-DO-nn`, tuning knobs `DIAG_*` / `OVERLAY_*`, all in the later sections. Tags follow the sibling GDDs: `[REF]` = in `docs/engine-reference/godot/`; `[UNV]` = unverified against the engine (the reference has **no** scripting, core, export or debugging file, so export presets and filters, feature tags, `OS.has_feature`, `OS.is_debug_build`, the `Performance` singleton, `Viewport.get_render_info`, `EngineDebugger` and multi-window `Window` are all `[UNV]`, knowledge-gap risk HIGH for 4.5 to 4.7); `[PLACEHOLDER]` = invented here, carrying a range and a proposed registry name, final nowhere. "-> ADR candidate" marks an implementation choice this GDD does not make. Every name from another GDD is used verbatim; a sibling's *provisional* name is cited with its source line and the word "provisional" and is never restated as a fact. Each rule gives the *Rule*, the *Why* and the acceptance-criteria group that proves it. Where a specialist proposal and a ruling differed, a one-line "(orchestrator ruling: ...)" note says which was taken.
136	
137	**Reading order.** Authority and gate: DO-1 (display only), DO-2 (build gate and source root), DO-3 (one subscriber), DO-9 (no sim state). Structure and layer: DO-4 (model/view), DO-5 (layer 4). Modes, input and viewer: DO-6 to DO-8, DO-10. Kernel states and boundaries: DO-11, DO-32 to DO-34. The channel and page contract: DO-12 to DO-15, DO-26. Reads, hashes, timings and counters: DO-16 to DO-19. The true/perceived pair and the discriminator: DO-20 to DO-23. The Sanity and Attention pages: DO-24, DO-25. Presentation, inertness, the Never list and evidence: DO-27 to DO-31. The non-screen observer sink and the defect ring: DO-35 *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The channel contract, classifier and seven page tables follow the rules.
138	
139	**DO-1. Display-only `DIAGNOSTIC` reader.** *Rule:* The Overlay is a kernel subscriber of class `DIAGNOSTIC`. It reads views and the kernel's diagnostics surface and writes nothing. It submits no command, calls no mutator, calls no owner's debug write function, and owns no block, no hook, no read view and no RNG stream. `force_stage`, `force_level`, Suit forcing and runtime-knob changes (honoured at P6, kern:734) belong to the owners' debug APIs, reached from the dev console (owed by the lead-programmer; kern:734, player-controller-input.md:742, suit-and-equipment.md:1317) behind the DO-2 gate; the Overlay only *displays* their result (a `FORCED` tag, DO-24). *Why:* kern:117 ("Subscriber handlers run with writes disabled... `INPUT_SURFACE` is the one class that may submit"); kern:203 row 11 ("Neither gets submit or mutators"); CR-9. A button that forced a stage would make the Overlay a write surface and break CR-9's `WriteScope` rule. *(orchestrator ruling: display only. Routed: Sanity's own row, sn:1352, lists `force_stage` / `force_level` beside the Overlay; a one-clause clarification is requested, "reached from the dev console, displayed by the Overlay". The tension between a debug-only `force_*` and CR-9 is the kernel owner's question and exists regardless of this GDD.)* *AC group:* inertness, gating.
140	
141	**DO-2. One gate, one dev source root.** *Rule:* All Overlay code, scenes, the world debug-draw node and the Overlay's dev actions live under **two source roots** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* `[PLACEHOLDER]`, final paths owned by architecture: the **observer root** `src/observer/` (the Overlay model, view, the observer sink and the Overlay's own dev actions: the only dev code the playtest preset includes; proposed registry name `observer_source_root`) and the **dev root** `src/debug/` (every other dev seam: `force_*`, the dev console, the dev input logger, the tree-walk script, the flash-scan tool and the owner-side channel providers; proposed registry name `overlay_source_root`). The public release excludes both roots and the playtest preset excludes only `src/debug/`, by export resource filters `[UNV, HIGH]`. The Overlay has its own root so that the playtest preset never needs a nested include of a folder inside an excluded one: Godot's precedence for that case is `[UNV]`, and if it were wrong the failure would be silent and unsafe (testers would receive `force_*` and the console). **Owner-side providers** (the code a system writes to implement `pull()` and its `draws[]` callbacks) live under `src/debug/<system>/`, never in the owner's runtime module, and the Input Adapter registers the dev actions through a dev-only seam `register_dev_forwarder` (requested of the Controller, OQ-DO-6), so no runtime module names a dev path outside that seam. The composition root registers the `DIAGNOSTIC` subscription entry point and the dev-only actions **only** when the dev predicate holds: the built-in `editor` feature or the custom feature tag `dev` (placeholders, `[UNV]`; a custom tag reads false in an editor run, so the predicate includes `editor`, verified in S-2). A second custom tag, `playtest`, selects the playtest preset (DO-6), which registers the `DIAGNOSTIC` subscription, the observer sink and the single action `debug_overlay_mark`, and nothing else (`debug_overlay_reveal` is dev-only) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R16)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* A CI step lists the public release export's files and fails the build on any path under either root; a second step compares the playtest export's file list to the playtest allow-list as an exact set (AC-DO-170). "Zero cost in Release" therefore means *nothing loaded*, not a runtime branch. **Load discipline:** the composition root loads the Overlay root only through a runtime `load()` guarded by `ResourceLoader.exists()` on the dev-root path; no `preload`, no `class_name` and no scene or resource reference to a dev-root path exists outside the dev root, and the dev root itself declares no `class_name` (a `preload` or a `class_name` in the filtered root breaks the release export, including through a stale global class cache). Lint AC-DO-172; a release export booted with the root absent is AC-DO-171. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The gate, the root and the CI step are **shared** by every dev seam guarded elsewhere (`force_*`, `--filter-test-freeze-dither`, `IA_PHANTOM_PROBE`, the dev input-event logger, the tree-walk script and the flash-scan tool, the dev console, the Input Adapter's `PC_*` presentation-diagnostics surface and its `debug_overlay_*` action registration); proposed registry name `overlay_build_gate`, and one versioned list of known dev artefacts (proposed `dev_artifact_list`) that every file-list check reuses. *Why:* six already-written acceptance criteria inspect the release export **file list**, not a runtime branch: kern:916, pipe:1028, AC-PF-79 (pf:1846), player-controller-input.md:1071, AC-AT-66 (at:1572) and AC-SN-85. A runtime `if OS.is_debug_build()` fails all six, and a flag can be flipped and still ship the oracle (Pillar 4, R-7). The same root makes the lints that allow-list "the Debug Overlay" implementable (AC-AT-66, AC-PF-51, AC-SN-74, AC-SN-146). *(orchestrator ruling: file-level exclusion plus gated registration; a runtime flag alone and a separate-project conditional compile were rejected, GDScript having no `#if`.)* *Engine gap:* export filters and feature tags are `[UNV, HIGH]`; one spike story (release-export an empty scene plus one file under the root, list the files, record `OS.has_feature` results in editor, dev export, playtest export and release export, and the tag semantics of each). -> ADR candidate (debug-gate / export-filter). *AC group:* absence and gating.
142	
143	**DO-3. Exactly one subscriber.** *Rule:* There is one `DIAGNOSTIC` subscription for the whole Overlay, with the DO-12 channel registry behind it, and therefore one entry point to strip. The handler only **copies** the P5 notification batch `(block_id, tick, change_keys)` (CR-10) and marks the model dirty (one batch per block per tick in a normal frame; in a catch-up frame, one merged batch per block, stamped with the frame's last tick and carrying the union of its change keys, because the Overlay is a `DIAGNOSTIC` subscriber and the kernel's ratified R-12 merges `PRESENTATION`, `PROJECTOR` and `DIAGNOSTIC` batches per catch-up frame, 2026-10-27; the batch feeds only the dirty-key accounting of DO-18, every other figure is read from the kernel `diagnostics` accessor or the owners' views, so the Overlay depends on no intermediate tick's batch) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*; it does no formatting, no classification and no I/O. TellAudit (AT-15) stays Attention's own `DIAGNOSTIC` fixture; the Overlay only displays its result (DO-25). *Why:* one entry point to exclude from release (DO-2); handlers must be cheap (kern:114); a handler that aborts on an engine script error is isolated by the kernel's best-effort completion sentinel (CR-19(b)): the handler returns `ctx.complete()`, a call that returns without it is recorded `INCOMPLETE` against the subscriber id and the kernel stays `RUNNING` with `T` advanced; engine script errors cannot be intercepted (CR-19(c)), so isolation is best-effort plus lint. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: replaces the kern:867 'throwing subscriber' wording, which CR-19 superseded)* *(orchestrator ruling: one subscriber, not one per panel or per system.)* *AC group:* gating, panel-fault isolation.
144	
145	**DO-4. Model/view split, pure model.** *Rule:* A pure `OverlayModel` (no scene tree) is built from `(diagnostics snapshot, read views, registered channels)`; an `OverlayView` Control tree pulls from the model at render rate. The classifier and every formula are model functions, unit-testable headless under `tests/unit/debug_overlay/`. The model holds **copies**, never a live reference to a block (GDScript has no const references, so a read-only view over a block is a copy or a frozen wrapper; kernel OQ 8). The model performs **no `FileAccess` I/O**: observer-log lines go to an injected `ObserverSink` (seam T-7) that owns every file operation, so the model stays headless-testable and DO-4's purity holds (AC-DO-186) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. This GDD describes behaviour (what is pure, what is cached, what is copied), not class code. -> ADR candidate (node and class layout, copy strategy). *Why:* testability (coding standards: dependency injection over singletons); writes-disabled is a kernel-enforced property, not the Overlay's; the Overlay must not hold a reference that could be mutated through. *AC group:* classifier, pages.
146	
147	**DO-5. Layer 4, the truth channel.** *Rule:* The view is a root-viewport `CanvasLayer` at pipeline layer 4, integer-scaled at the HUD scale (`H_default = max(k, 3)`, pipe:224 (PR-12), pipe:373) plus the placeholder `OVERLAY_SCALE_OFFSET`, above the HUD (layer 2) and chart table and menus (layer 3). It receives **no** Filter pass, no lighting, no camera jolt and no grade (pipe:102; pf:223 row 9: the pass sits below every `CanvasLayer`, the frame is fed nothing). It carries no Filter-fed value except the `perceived` column, which is labelled as perceived. Non-interactive panels use `MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE`; the Overlay never takes gameplay focus (4.6 dual focus `[REF modules/ui.md]`; the 4.5 recursive mouse-filter behaviour is also in the reference). **Process model** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the Overlay root and its model driver run with `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` and never depend on `SceneTree.paused`; the numeral refresh, the class fold and the view update run from the Overlay's own `_process`, so a paused game (the kernel `PAUSED`, or a tree paused by a menu) stays inspectable. `Engine.time_scale` scales the process delta that accumulates toward the next numeral refresh, so numerals refresh more slowly in slow motion, but **neither `Engine.time_scale` nor the refresh throttle ever changes a classification**, because the class fold and every counter run on kernel ticks (DO-21). The Overlay's `process_priority` is set after the kernel's TickDriver node (CR-1a), so a refresh reads committed state. *Why:* the truth channel must not itself be corruptible (Pillar 1); the Overlay is one of the surfaces the Filter pass never reaches (pf:223 row 9). *AC group:* palette, gating, focus.
148	
149	**DO-6. Four modes and two presets.** (registry: `overlay_modes`) *Rule:* `OFF` (registered, handler returns at once, nothing collected), `FULL` (all pages), `OBSERVER_STRIP` (one line, DO-7) and `HIDDEN` (subscribed and collecting the observer set only, drawing nothing; DO-35); transitions in States and Transitions. A mode change takes effect within one rendered frame and never alters `T`. **Two export presets, one source tree** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: the **dev preset** (the full dev root under the dev predicate of DO-2) launches `OFF` by default, or `HIDDEN` with the launch option placeholder `--overlay=hidden`, and registers every dev action. The **playtest preset** is the release template plus the custom feature tag `playtest`: the composition root forces `HIDDEN` at launch whatever the command line says (a store or double-click launch cannot pass an option, so tester safety no longer depends on one), registers **only** `debug_overlay_mark` (no `reveal`, no `toggle`, no `mode`, no `dump`), so a tester session can never leave `HIDDEN` (Resolved 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R16, OQ-DO-30 option A: `debug_overlay_reveal` is dev-only and absent from the playtest export's action map), and starts the observer sink (DO-35). The playtest export contains the Overlay root and the sink but none of the other dev seams (`force_*`, the dev console, the dev input logger); an allow-list check of its own file list is AC-DO-170. The user confirmed the release template as the base of the playtest preset on 2026-10-27 (D97); that the kernel `diagnostics` accessor exists in it is still verified in spike S-2 and recorded in the debug-gate ADR *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* (fallback if the accessor is absent from the release template: the debug template with the same tag). *Why:* X-BS-11, AC-BS-122 and AC-SN-88 need an observer read that is never shown to the tester. *(orchestrator ruling, revised at design review: the earlier "a playtest build is a dev build launched `HIDDEN`; there is no third build flavour in MVP" is replaced by a preset; it is still one source tree and one code path. Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): the playtest export preset is confirmed (D97, OQ-DO-25), and the earlier "no third build flavour in MVP" ruling is superseded by the user.)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* *AC group:* modes and observer.
150	
151	**DO-7. Observer strip and the oracle rule.** *Rule:* `OBSERVER_STRIP` is one text line: `T`, kernel state, Attention `phase`, the viewer's sanity `stage` and hash status (`OK` / `n/a` / `DRIFT` plus the age of `hash_T`). It also shows the sticky `defects seen` count of DO-35 (a number, no ref), the `unverified` count and the coverage digits (`intent n/N, leak-probe n/N, bypass-probe n/N`, DO-21 (5)(v); numbers only, no ref) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. It shows no ledger field, no true/perceived pair and no ref; the hash status is the age of `hash_T` with the algorithm tag as DO-17 defines it (the kernel's `hash_algo` field, granted 2026-10-27; `H64 (algo untagged; SHA-256/8)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)* only if it is absent). `FULL` and the strip are **tester-hostile**: a tester's screen, recording or stream must never carry either (the strip names the stage and the phase). `HIDDEN` is only safe because leaving it needs the reveal chord (DO-8), which exists in the dev preset only; in the playtest preset no action leaves `HIDDEN` at all *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R16)*. In a measured playtest session the strip is not used at all: the observer reads the log (DO-35). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *Why:* sn:174 calls the ledger "a deliberate Pillar 4 oracle risk"; the Overlay is the only reader outside `sanity/` (AC-SN-74). The risk is a process risk the code can only mitigate, not remove, and the GDD says so plainly. *AC group:* modes and observer (the strip contains no ref and no ledger field; `HIDDEN` draws no Overlay node).
152	
153	**DO-8. Toggle input path and reveal chord.** *Rule:* The Controller's Input Adapter registers the Overlay's dev-only actions only under the DO-2 dev predicate (in the playtest preset only `debug_overlay_mark`, DO-6; `debug_overlay_reveal` and its chords are dev-only, delegated ruling R16) and forwards them to the Overlay by a host-local call: never a command, never a binding-table entry visible to Settings, never in the rebinding or accessibility enumerations. Placeholder names (registry: `debug_overlay_actions`): `debug_overlay_toggle`, `debug_overlay_page_next`, `debug_overlay_page_prev`, `debug_overlay_mode`, `debug_overlay_dump`, and two added here, `debug_overlay_reveal` and `debug_overlay_mark`, and three for selection: `debug_overlay_cursor_next`, `debug_overlay_cursor_prev` (move a row cursor over the current page's selectable rows: refs and the viewer row on `P-TRUTH`, channels and draw toggles on `P-CHANNELS`) and `debug_overlay_activate` (pin or unpin the ref under the cursor, cycle the viewer, select the channel, flip the draw toggle); all three act only in `FULL`. Placeholder defaults *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: F5 to F8 moved off the editor's run, pause and stop shortcuts)*: toggle F3, page next and previous F4 and Shift+F4, mode cycle Insert, dump Home, mark End, cursor next and previous PageDown and PageUp, activate Delete, reveal chord Ctrl+Shift+F3; gamepad: the reveal chord is both stick clicks (L3 + R3, as the Controller records it), recognised by a **stateful detector in the Adapter** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: both clicks must be down within a 0.5 s chord window of each other, held 0.5 s, fire once, and re-arm only after both are released (the Adapter counts these in its own injected frame deltas; the Overlay reads no clock); other gamepad bindings `[PLACEHOLDER]`; every default is verified against the editor's shortcuts and the Controller's gameplay table `[UNV]` (OQ-DO-6). The row cursor is dev-session state (DO-9), wraps at the ends of the page's selectable rows, and `activate` on a row with no action is ignored. In `HIDDEN` only the reveal chord (dev preset only; the playtest preset registers no `reveal`, R16) and `mark` act: the chord reveals to `OBSERVER_STRIP`, not `FULL`; `mark` is accepted silently and echoed to the log (DO-35). From `OBSERVER_STRIP` the same chord leads to `FULL` with the history preserved, the only route from the strip to `FULL`, so a stray `toggle` never clears history. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Matching** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: every binding uses exact-match semantics (`InputEvent.is_match(event, true)`), so Shift+F4 never also fires F4 and Ctrl+Shift+F3 never also fires `toggle` (which could clear the history the chord was meant to reveal); the Adapter resolves one event to one action, longest modifier set first, and ignores echo events (`event.is_echo()`), so a held key never repeats an action. The actions are `StringName` action names and use `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_*`, not `device == 0` `[REF breaking-changes.md 4.7]`. *Why:* the Controller lint "no `Input` reads outside the Adapter" (player-controller-input.md:58 PC-1, :1026); a tester brushing the plain toggle must not reveal the oracle. *(orchestrator ruling: the Adapter-forwarded dev action set, plus the reveal chord, the mark action and the three selection actions as refinements; the Controller-owner amendment request grows by five action names and joins the open lint collision at player-controller-input.md:1097.)* *AC group:* input path, enumeration negatives.
154	
155	**DO-9. Dev-session state only.** *Rule:* Mode, page, row cursor, selected viewer, selected ref, pinned refs, observer marks, the defect ring (DO-35) and every history window are dev-session state: never a block, never in a snapshot, never in `state_hash`, never saved across launches in MVP (a dev `ConfigFile` under `user://` is deferred, Open Questions). *Why:* a persisted Overlay block would enter `state_hash` and break the G4 comparison with the Overlay on versus off (AC-AT-56 shape). *AC group:* inertness.
156	
157	**DO-10. One viewer.** *Rule:* The Overlay has one selectable viewer `PlayerId`, defaulting to the local seat (MVP: PlayerId 1) and always shown in the header; the operator cycles it with `activate` on the viewer row of `P-TRUTH`, reached with `cursor_next` / `cursor_prev` (DO-8), and each cycle resets the per-`(ref, viewer)` counters (AC-DO-77). Addressing is by `PlayerId`, never `peer_id` (pf:271, PF-10). Because the Filter answers for the **local seat only** and returns the honest record for a remote `PlayerId` while counting `remote_queries` (PF-10), the Overlay **never calls `perceived` for a remote seat**: a viewer other than the local seat classifies `UNAVAILABLE` with reason `REMOTE_VIEWER`, and `P-TRUTH` shows "perceived: not queried". This keeps `remote_queries` a pure leakage indicator and prevents a seat-B lie from classifying `HONEST` against its own honest-record answer. Vertical Slice B adds a seat cycler (contract only, DO-34). *(orchestrator ruling: one selectable viewer, refined by the finding that the Filter answers for the local seat only, PF-10.)* *AC group:* classifier, viewer switch.
158	
159	**DO-11. Behaviour in every kernel state.** *Rule:* The Overlay is drawable in all six kernel states (table in States and Transitions). In a dev build `FAULTED` halts the kernel with diagnostics (kern:151); the render loop and the Overlay keep running and show the FAULT record `(T, type, issuer, host_order, block_id, assertion)` while the kernel is not ticking (chart-table-web-map-and-menus.md:377 accepts "Dev builds halt with the Debug Overlay (not ours)" as written). `BOOTING` shows boot progress and, on failure, the unknown `hook_id` or the cycle path (kern:606). `HIDDEN` stays hidden even on `FAULTED`: a tester must not see it either. *Why:* the Overlay is the tool one reaches for when the kernel is least healthy. *AC group:* kernel states.
160	
161	**DO-12. Channel registration contract.** *Rule:* Every system that wants a diagnostics presence registers a **channel** at composition-root time under the DO-2 tag. A channel declares the fields in the contract table below (proposed registry name `diag_panel_contract`). **Entry point** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the single registration call is `register_channel(declaration: Dictionary) -> Dictionary` on the Overlay's composition-root facade, valid only while the kernel is `BOOTING` and returning `{ok: bool, reason: String}`, where `reason` is a `DIAG_ERR` value (DO-14) or `LATE_REGISTRATION`, the one registration-time reason outside `DIAG_ERR` (a refused call, not a faulting channel: it raises no `DEFECT` row); a call after `BOOTING` returns `{ok: false, reason: "LATE_REGISTRATION"}` and the channel is `REJECTED`. The Overlay renders whatever is registered on the generic page `P-CHANNELS` and restates no owner's name as a fact. *Why:* it closes the three open asks "the Debug Overlay GDD should freeze the names" (pipe:1055, player-controller-input.md:1095, interaction-system.md:731) as **owners freeze their own names, using this convention**, and honours Body's "use the exact diagnostic names above" (ship-body-and-interior-physics.md:898) by construction. Freezing six systems' tables here would repeat the 2026-10-26 placeholder-becomes-fact failure and go stale on the first sibling edit. Transport and format of any diagnostics pipeline stay the AT-32 ADR candidate. *(orchestrator ruling: panel contract and naming convention here; names stay with their owners.)* *AC group:* channel contract.
162	
163	**DO-13. Naming convention and severity vocabulary.** *Rule:* Channel and row names are snake_case `<system>_<noun>` or the owner's existing prefix (`PC_*`, `IA_*`, `BDY_*`, `graph_*`, `diag.*`, all provisional where their owner says so). Units are in the declaration, never in the name; a counter name does not end in `_ms` or `_us` unless the owner's registry name already does. The severity vocabulary is fixed at four levels: `OK`, `NOTE`, `WARN`, `DEFECT` (registry: `diag_severity_vocabulary`). A row declares its severity as a rule over its own value (for example "`> 0` is `WARN`"); the Overlay evaluates the rule and never invents one for an owner. A `DEFECT` rule must cite the owner's rule it enforces. *Why:* this resolves the mismatch between the brief's `OK/WARN/DEFECT` and `OK/NOTE/DEFECT`. Severity is always a text tag and colour is secondary (DO-27). *AC group:* channel contract.
164	
165	**DO-14. Per-panel fault isolation as validated results.** *Rule:* GDScript has no exceptions: a script error aborts the function it occurs in and, under `-d`, stops the debugger (kernel CR-19(c)), so a channel fault is defined as an **invalid result**, never as a catch. Every channel `pull()` returns a plain Dictionary `{channel_id, rows, complete}`, and every page render consumes only validated data. The Overlay validates each result and each registration against a **closed error enum `DIAG_ERR`**: `NULL_RESULT` (null; also what an aborted `pull()` returns), `NOT_A_DICTIONARY`, `SCHEMA_MISMATCH` (a missing or mistyped field, an unknown row kind or an unknown severity word), `LIMIT_EXCEEDED` (`DIAG_ROWS_PER_CHANNEL_MAX` or a text or table cap), `INVALID_CALLABLE` (`Callable.is_valid()` false at registration or at call time) and `INCOMPLETE` (`complete` is not `true`: the kernel's completion-sentinel convention, CR-19(b)). The failing channel shows one `DEFECT` row naming its `channel_id` and the `DIAG_ERR` value, and after `DIAG_PANEL_ERR_LATCH_N` consecutive failures the channel is suspended until the next mode change. Real script errors (a nested helper that errors, a null dereference) are printed by the engine and belong to the debugger and to CI, which fails on any engine `ERROR` line in a dev run; the Overlay claims no more than the kernel does (best-effort plus lint). An expected channel not yet registered during `BOOTING` shows `PENDING`, and after `BOOTING` shows `NOTE absent`; a channel with no update for `DIAG_CHANNEL_STALE_S` shows `STALE` (`NOTE`). A diagnostics tool must not take the build down. *Why:* the kernel's fault channel (CR-19) is the precedent and replaced the earlier 'throws' model for the same reason; kern:867's old 'throwing subscriber' wording is superseded by CR-19, so no cross-document escalation is outstanding. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* *AC group:* panel fault.
166	
167	**DO-15. Page set.** *Rule:* Seven MVP pages, each specified as a data table of (row, source, unit, cadence, severity rule), below: `P-KERNEL`, `P-HOOKS`, `P-STATE`, `P-TRUTH`, `P-SANITY`, `P-ATTENTION`, `P-FRAME`. Every other system appears only as a registered channel on the generic page `P-CHANNELS` (a channel list plus the selected channel's rows and its world debug-draw toggles); that is not an eighth designed panel. Page order is fixed and `page_next` / `page_prev` cycle `P-KERNEL` to `P-FRAME` and then `P-CHANNELS`. No page designs a layout; layout is the view's affair. *Why:* the seven pages cover the six routed items (hash, dirty keys, hook timings, the Graph `true_value`, Attention level, sanity per player) plus the PF-41 contract and the Pipeline surface while keeping a system sized S. *AC group:* pages.
168	
169	**DO-16. Reads only published names.** *Rule:* The Overlay reads a system only through that system's published read view or diagnostics channel: Graph `true_value(kind, id)`, `block_hash()`, `summary()`, `failures(filter)`, `compartment(cid)`, `power_use(section_id)` (lsg:199); Suit `true_value(key, player_id)` (SE-29); Sanity `sanity_view(player_id)`, `sanity.state`, `sanity.ledger` (SN-28, **sn:335-337**, cited as the paragraph, not the bare sn:336); Attention `attention.state`, `attention.view`; Horror `horror.view`; the Filter's `perceived` and the PF-41 counters. It never reaches into a block it does not own a view of. The ledger is `HOST_ONLY` (provisional on a mirror, DO-34): on a `MIRROR` the ledger is unreadable and rows needing it classify `UNAVAILABLE` with reason `NO_LEDGER`. *Why:* the ledger lint (AC-SN-74) names the Overlay as the one non-Sanity reader; the Overlay is the sole sanctioned `true_value` caller beside the Filter (AC-PF-51). *AC group:* gating (lint), cross-system.
170

171	**DO-17. Hash display: locked versus provisional.** *Rule:* The Overlay shows the kernel's `state_hash` exactly as last published, with `hash_T` (the tick it was computed at), its age `T - hash_T` and the algorithm tag. **`hash_algo` is not a kernel-published name** (the kernel names only `H64`, kern:531, D.12; the kernel text "xxHash64 or FNV-1a 64, pending ADR" is **superseded**: H64 is ratified as the first 8 bytes of SHA-256 (user ruling X13, R-17) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)*; a search of the kernel GDD finds no `hash_algo`): it was a **field this GDD requested** in the P-9 accessor (DO-33a), granted by the kernel 2026-10-27; if it is absent the algorithm cell reads `H64 (algo untagged; SHA-256/8)` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings, consistency follow-up)*. With the field present, a hash from another `hash_algo` is never compared. The per-block column is the owner-published `block_hash()` where one exists (Graph LS-19 and LS-21, Emitter `block_hash()`, Layout `layout_hash`) and `n/a` otherwise; if the kernel adopts K-1 (a per-block cached hash, **routed, not adopted**, lsg:1155; sl:1290) the column switches to the kernel's per-block hash (P-10). The Overlay **never hashes anything itself**, on a timer or on demand. The cadence is the kernel's (DO-33). *Why:* K-1 is "routed, not adopted; D.12 stands until the kernel owner amends" (lsg:1155), and OQ-17 (sl:1316) warns that a GDScript 64-bit hash over 100 to 300 KiB may exceed 1.5 ms, so a hash per tick would put 90 ms of hashing into every real second. *Split:* the `state_hash` formula (kern D.12) is locked; per-block hashing and the cadence are provisional. *(orchestrator ruling: the kernel computes, the Overlay displays.)* *AC group:* pages (hash), unblocked sibling ACs (kern:915).

173	**DO-18. Dirty-key accounting with peak-hold.** *Rule:* In the P5 batch the handler records, per delivered batch `(block_id, tick)`, the key count (or an `ALL` collapse, kern D.9). In a normal frame that is one sample per tick; in a catch-up frame (kernel R-12, ratified by the user 2026-10-27) it is one merged sample stamped with the frame's last tick whose keys are the union over the frame's ticks, so it can read higher than any single tick did and can collapse to `ALL` where no single tick would; such a collapse is `WARN`, never `DEFECT` (the merge is legal kernel behaviour, not a fault), and the Overlay does not try to reconstruct per-tick counts. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)* Each refresh the model folds the batches delivered since the last refresh into `last`, `peak` and `collapse_count` per block. `dirty_load_pm` (Formulas) is shown against `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS` 256, **never altered**. An `ALL` collapse is `WARN`, not `DEFECT`: it is legal kernel behaviour, and a restore legitimately produces one `ALL` then silence. The Graph's measured worst cases (about 38 keys MVP, about 135 VS-A, lsg:201 LS-20) are the reference points. Every `DEFECT`-capable counter and timing is **peak-held** across the folded ticks, never sampled: numerals refresh at `DIAG_REFRESH_HZ` (10) but the kernel emits at `TICK_RATE` 60 and the Graph hooks run on ticks 6n, 6n + 2 and 6n + 4 *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, so a one-tick spike would otherwise fall between refreshes. *Why:* a cadence-blind display would hide the very events it exists to catch. *AC group:* pages (dirty keys, peak-hold).
